title: Quirk dossier and mini-probe plays
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick working doc to capture small, repeatable customer friction patterns (the "quirks") and propose micro-probes we can run in a single sprint. Meant for PM/SE pairing and fast validation with 3–5 customers.
- Not a full synthesis (we have larger VOC docs). This is tactical: find low-effort, high-clarity fixes or clarifying experiments that shrink support volume or unblock purchase decisions.

High-level constraints:
- Probes should be implementable with <= 5 dev days (or config + docs + SE playbook).
- Target metric: reduce CS tickets on that theme by 25% in 8 weeks OR increase committed dedicated deals by moving a single objection off the table.
- Prefer solutions that don't require a model architecture change (runtime/config, console UX, docs, SDK).

Observed quirk clusters (raw notes) 
1) "Why is my latency spiky when the token length is small?"
   - Customers: 3 enterprise SaaS, 2 startups. Examples in tickets CS-2389, CS-2401.
   - Symptoms: steady trough latency but occasional 200–400ms spikes for short prompt calls (20–80 tokens).
   - Hypothesis: routing to cold worker or batch-coalescing behavior + default autoscaling window. Also sometimes fallback to suboptimal kernel on small sequences.
   - Quick probe ideas:
     a) instrument sample traces and add a short (1ms) synthetic warm-up before first token to test cold start sensitivity (SE-run A/B).
     b) expose 'prefer-warm-worker' flag in Dedicated config for a small subset of customers to keep 1 worker hot.
     c) console note + product doc explaining expected variance and how to tune pooling.

2) "Model outputs are inconsistent after we enabled caching / KV"
   - Customers: 2 mid-market, 1 fintech. Ticket examples: CS-2361.
   - Symptom: output occasionally drops context when early-bail caching used; customers think it's a regression.
   - Hypothesis: prefix cache invalidation semantics not obvious at SDK layer; prompt templating plus session reuse leads to dropped tokens on variant models.
   - Probe ideas:
     a) add an SDK helper: cache_scope = 'conversation' vs 'prompt' and produce a small diff log when cache returns partial context. (Engineer: Samir Rao)
     b) create a short KB article with annotated example showing how to design prompts for prefix cache.
     c) add a telemetry tag so we can count cache-hit vs semantic-mismatch errors in Console.

3) "Embeddings drift across model upgrades"
   - Customers: search and sem-sim teams, 4 customers. Concern: vector distances change after auto-upgrade to new embedding model.
   - Hypothesis: nightly auto-upgrades + different embedding space; customers doing offline reindexing can't afford silent swaps.
   - Probe ideas:
     a) set up a "pin and notify" flow in the Console: customers can opt-in to immediate upgrade or be notified with a diff sandbox (small sample).
     b) add an API call embeddings.compare_sample(old_model, new_model, sample_ids) that returns drift score. (Minimal backend lift: run sample batch in isolated runner).
     c) doc + release checklist for index teams.

Candidate micro-probes (prioritized)
- P1: "Prefer-hot-worker" flag pilot (probe duration: 2 weeks; owner: infra/serving runtime SE; rough effort: 3 dev days + 1 SRE day). Goal: demonstrate spike reduction on short prompts for 5 customers. Linked ticket: CS-2412.
- P2: SDK cache-scope helper + sample KB (probe duration: 1 week dev + docs; owner: devx). Goal: reduce 'dropped context' tickets by surfacing mismatch.
- P3: Embedding drift sample runner (probe duration: 2 dev days + 1 product review). Owner: research/embeddings. Goal: give a measurable drift score for customers before upgrade.
- P4: "Graceful fallback policy" templated config: if a warmed variant is not available, prefer a lower-quantized model rather than cold start. (2 dev days + policy doc). Owner: serving-runtime.

Experiment design snippets (practical)
- Warm-worker pilot A/B:
  - N=5 customers (mix: 2 startups, 3 enterprise).
  - Traffic: mirror 10% to pilots. Measure p50/p95/p99 for short token requests. Baseline: last 14 days.
  - Success criteria: p95 reduction >= 20% and ticket threads mentioning 'spike' drop in followup.

- SDK cache-scope telemetry:
  - instrument a lightweight enum in SDK that adds header X-Cache-Scope and a short log when a cache-return seems to drop prompt tokens (heuristic).
  - Capture counts in Console and send weekly digest to CS.

Notes on comms and SE playbook snippets:
- For embedding drift: prepare a one-pager for search teams: "How to stage embedding upgrades" with checklist: pin indexes, run compare_sample, reindex threshold.
- For warm-worker: prepare a short FAQ for procurement: "Does prefer-hot increase cost?" with back-of-envelope cost: 1 hot worker ≈ +10–15% on committed throughput for small workloads; recommend A/B only for accounts with >500 qps short-burst patterns.

Open questions / decision needs
- Priority: are we okay shipping 'prefer-hot-worker' as an undocumented flag first (SE pilot) or should it go through PM review + advisory note? (Product ask: quick pilot is preferred).
- Metrics: CS needs fast visibility—can Console surface a simple "quirk dashboard" with top-10 quirk tags? Minimal MVP would ingest a telemetry tag and surface counts. Effort? (obs team input needed).
- Billing implications: prefer-hot may change unit economics for hosted customers — finance check required before public launch.

Next steps / owners
- Lena: draft pilot experiment ticket for prefer-hot-worker (due 2025-05-21).
- Evan: prototype SDK cache-scope helper and add heuristic logs (due 2025-05-28).
- Priya: write the embedding upgrade one-pager and contact 2 customers for pilot (due 2025-05-23).
- Schedule 30m sync with serving-runtime + infra + obs on 2025-05-20 to align on telemetry and rollout guardrails.

Appendix: example customer note (redacted)
- "We've been seeing weird jumps in latency — sometimes a single request that should return in 40ms goes to 320ms. It's killing our snappy chat use case. We haven't changed prompts. Is there a warm-up you can run?" — Customer ACME Search, support thread #4232

Rough ticket mapping (for quick reference)
- CS-2389: short-token spikes (log + trace attached)
- CS-2361: cache/dropped-context examples
- CS-2412: request for worker affinity pilot (customer ask)

Notes-to-self:
- Keep probes as experiments, not product promises. We want signal quickly and reversible changes.
- Aim to fold successful probes into docs/Console features and then mark them as product to-be-scoped.

End of doc.
